- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +2–4% above peak.
- If event net supply is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer.
- When sentiment alternates between bullish/bearish (e.g., 0.33/1.00), model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and net supply < -10, model tends to overfit recent highs; apply mean reversion to 10–15% of recent 18d average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and event supply is negative, model underestimates price drop; add 1–2% downward adjustment.
- When sentiment is high and event supply is negative, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per event day.
